extracted.intended_audience: Hospitals, health systems, ambulatory surgical centers (ASCs), hospital administrators, payers, and other stakeholders participating in or evaluating CMS's Transforming Episode Accountability Model (TEAM)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the criteria, definitions, and proposed methodological rules CMS is using or proposing for TEAM target price construction, baseline and update methodologies, risk adjustment, reconciliation, and related requests for information (ASC and POH). Relevant to entities required to implement, evaluate, or comment on TEAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sliding historical CQS baseline methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to transition from fixed CQS baseline periods to sliding historical CQS baseline periods (with a change from calendar year to July–June timeframe for certain measures) to better support ongoing quality improvement and maintain relevant performance benchmarks throughout the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS seeks comment on adopting this sliding historical CQS baseline approach (proposed at §512.547(a)(1)-(5)), whether transition should begin in TEAM PY2 rather than PY1, and whether fixed historical or concurrent baseline methodologies (each with July–June timeframes) would be preferable. Also seeks comment on whether concurrent methodology implementation should begin in PY1 or PY2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target price baseline and trend construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary target prices will be calculated using 3 years of rolling baseline episode spending, trended forward with 2 additional historical years to the performance year, at the level of MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region, with updates using performance year data during reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regions defined as nine U.S. census divisions; episode types based on TEAM episode categories (CABG, LEJR, Major Bowel, SHFFT, Spinal Fusion). CMS will modify preliminary target prices during reconciliation using performance year data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode spending winsorization/capping at 99th percentile
rubrics_metrics.description: Episode spending will be capped at the 99th percentile for each of the 29 MS-DRG/HCPCS episode types and 9 regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark price calculations use the average capped and standardized spending in the most recent baseline year dollars for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region (resulting in 261 benchmark prices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark price calculation by MS-DRG/HCPCS and region
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark price equals the average capped and standardized spending in the most recent baseline year dollars for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type in each region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark prices will be calculated using all hospitals in a region, regardless of TEAM participation status; results in 261 benchmark prices (29 episode types × 9 regions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of all hospitals in benchmark construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark prices are calculated using all hospitals in a region regardless of TEAM participation status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to produce robust benchmark prices; affects comparability and may avoid small-sample volatility for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of prospective trend and discount factors
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will apply a prospective trend factor and a discount factor to benchmark prices when constructing preliminary target prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During reconciliation, the trend will be updated (subject to a cap) and a normalization factor updated (subject to a cap); participant realized performance year case mix will be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment factors and components
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk adjustment factors include age group, Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) count, beneficiary economic risk, episode category-specific HCC adjusters, and hospital-level adjusters including a hospital bed size factor and a safety net hospital factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk adjustment factors are calculated at the MS-DRG/HCPCS level using a weighted linear regression where episodes are weighted by baseline year (baseline year 1 = 17%, year 2 = 33%, year 3 = 50%). These risk adjustment factors will be fixed and applied to performance year episodes at reconciliation based on the realized case mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting of baseline years for risk adjustment estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline episodes are weighted differentially based on whether they belong to baseline year 1, 2, or 3: 17%, 33%, and 50% respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These weights are used in the weighted linear regression that estimates risk adjustment parameters; weights were finalized in prior FY IPPS/LTCH final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization factor construction and cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Final normalization factor is calculated as the mean of the benchmark price for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region divided by the mean of the risk-adjusted benchmark price for the same MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is capped should this ratio exceed ±5 percent of the prospective normalization factor, per prior rulemaking. Purpose: ensure the average of the total risk-adjusted preliminary target price does not exceed average of total non-risk adjusted preliminary target price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective trend factor calculation and ±3% cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Final target prices include a retrospective trend factor, calculated as average capped performance year episode spending divided by the capped average baseline episode spending (national mean benchmark price), and capped at being within 3 percent of the prospective trend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The retrospective trend factor is intended to incorporate performance-year actual spending into reconciliation but is capped to limit instability; CMS considered removing the cap but did not propose to do so because it may introduce instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation (final) target price formula
rubrics_metrics.description: The reconciliation target price is calculated as the product of: capped mean baseline episode spending in the most recent baseline year dollars × discount factor × risk adjustment multiplier using the performance year case-mix × capped final normalization factor × capped retrospective trend factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants may receive reconciliation payments (after quality adjustments) if performance year spending is below the reconciliation target price, or owe a repayment if spending is above it.

rubrics_metrics.name: APC update factor definition and application
rubrics_metrics.description: APC update factor defined as the component applied to the prospective trend factor to ensure APC weights corresponding to the performance year calendar year are incorporated into final target price calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculated at the MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region level as the ratio of benchmark prices calculated with APC weights for the calendar year of the performance year to preliminary benchmark prices calculated with APC weights for the prior calendar year. It is applied as a multiplier to the prospective trend factor (creating an updated prospective trend factor) and the retrospective trend cap is set relative to the updated prospective trend factor. APC update factors would be calculated after publication of the CY OPPS/ASC final rule and shared with TEAM participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG update factor definition and Q4 episode handling
rubrics_metrics.description: MS-DRG update factor is the component applied to the prospective trend factor for episodes with anchor hospitalization/procedure end dates in the fourth quarter of the performance year to account for changes in MS-DRG definitions and weights between the first and second fiscal years in the performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculated at the MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region level as the ratio of benchmark prices calculated with the second fiscal year inputs to preliminary benchmark prices calculated with first fiscal year inputs. Applied as a multiplier to the prospective trend factor for Q4 episodes and shared after FY IPPS/LTCH final rule publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning first fiscal year MS-DRG for episodes in second fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: For episodes with anchor end dates in the fourth quarter (second fiscal year of a performance year), CMS proposes assigning a first fiscal year MS-DRG to those episodes for certain components (baseline-derived components).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline-derived components (benchmark price and risk adjustment coefficients) would be calculated using MS-DRG mappings and weights from the assigned first fiscal year; normalization and retrospective trend calculations would reflect assigned first and second FY MS-DRG combinations with explicit caps (normalization ±5% relative to prospective normalization for assigned first FY MS-DRG; retrospective trend ±3% of updated prospective trend factor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of episodes lacking preliminary benchmark prices due to mapping changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a non-TEAM MS-DRG in the first fiscal year maps to a TEAM MS-DRG in the second fiscal year (so preliminary benchmark prices and target price components would not be available), CMS proposes that TEAM participants would not be accountable for episodes with anchor end dates in the fourth quarter initiated by such anchor hospitalizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a proposed exception to avoid assigning accountability where necessary price components are unavailable; CMS provides mapping scenarios (see Table X.A-06) and seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision not to reissue multiple preliminary target prices
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considered, but is not proposing, to update and deliver preliminary target prices to TEAM participants for each calendar and fiscal year final rule (i.e., not issuing multiple preliminary prices per performance year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: managing multiple preliminary target prices would increase participant burden and pricing methodology complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision not to apply descaling/backwards mapping for Q4 episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considered, but is not proposing, to backwards map and descale spending for episodes with anchor end dates in the fourth quarter, which would apply a descaling factor to episode spending to adjust for MS-DRG weight changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although descaling could improve target price accuracy, CMS believes it would introduce complexity and implementation challenges; therefore, not proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to calculate prospective normalization factor using all baseline episodes (start PY2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting with performance year 2, CMS proposes to calculate the prospective normalization factor at the MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region level based on all applicable episodes in the baseline period (rather than only baseline year 3), applying risk adjustment coefficients to all baseline year episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: better predictive accuracy, better representation of all episodes used in benchmark price construction, and smoothing short-term fluctuations. Internal analysis found improved predictive accuracy and small differences versus using only the most recent baseline year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) inclusion RFI criteria/questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for information asking stakeholders for input on ASC participation in TEAM, including model structure, participant roles and financial accountability, episode and target price construction, and quality measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific questions include operational challenges for ASCs, readiness support, necessary programmatic waivers, which entity should be financially accountable for ASC-initiated episodes, accounting for financial/ownership relationships between hospitals and ASCs, barriers to hospital–ASC partnerships, opportunities for ASC efficiency gains, additional surgical episode types to consider, adapting beneficiary-level risk adjustment for multi-setting episodes, potential barriers to care for beneficiaries and mitigation, handling model overlap with other initiatives, and appropriate quality measures and comparability between ASCs and hospital outpatient departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital with Physician Ownership (POH) legal/regulatory considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of a POH and background on relevant statutory exceptions (Stark law §1877) including rural provider and whole hospital exceptions, applicable restrictions from the Affordable Care Act, and limits on expansion of POHs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS describes how exceptions work, grandfathering date rules, and the types of restrictions (e.g., prohibition on increasing operating rooms/procedure rooms/beds beyond licensed levels after specified dates) intended to avoid overutilization, patient steering, cherry-picking, and lemon-dropping. This section frames a request for information on POH issues in the context of TEAM.
